summary: Breaking the speed-monster wand reaches C's adjacent-monster effect, but JavaScript skips the call to bhitm() for that wand type. The resulting missing resistance draw is annotated as resist() in the queue; the first source defect is apply.c:do_break_wand() dispatch.

source.branch: When a broken wand is processed and an adjacent square contains a monster, apply.c:do_break_wand() calls bhitm(mon, obj) for every wand type. JavaScript currently calls bhitm() only for light, striking, polymorph, and teleportation wands, and records note_unported('zap.c bhitm') for other types.
callers: C apply.c:doapply() dispatches the WAND_CLASS item to do_break_wand().
JavaScript js/apply.js:doapply() dispatches WAND_CLASS to do_break_wand().
C apply.c:do_break_wand() calls zap.c:bhitm() for an adjacent surviving monster; JavaScript js/apply.js:do_break_wand() must preserve the same call for WAN_SPEED_MONSTER.
dependencies: zap.c:bhitm() already handles WAN_SPEED_MONSTER by calling resist(mon, otmp->oclass, 0, NOTELL), then adjusting speed on success.
js/zap.js:bhitm() already ports this WAN_SPEED_MONSTER branch, including resist() and mon_adjust_speed().

evidence: The saved accepted v64 evaluation at challenges/evaluations/accepted-6533e0a77d2145733c0fcabedf1e8446dc251fba-v64.json records 275/277 screens, 2629/2641 RNG calls, and 276/277 cursors for this recording; its first C RNG mismatch is rn2(105)=85 at resist(zap.c:6141), step 262.
Upstream apply.c:do_break_wand(), lines 4095-4096, calls bhitm(mon, obj) whenever m_at(x, y) finds an adjacent monster; no wand-type guard surrounds that callback.

JavaScript js/apply.js:do_break_wand(), lines 4910-4917, restricts bhitm() to WAN_LIGHT, WAN_STRIKING, WAN_POLYMORPH, and WAN_TELEPORTATION. For WAN_SPEED_MONSTER it records note_unported('zap.c bhitm') and does not make the call.

Upstream zap.c:bhitm(), lines 230-240, and JavaScript js/zap.js:bhitm(), lines 3403-3415, both implement WAN_SPEED_MONSTER through resist(..., 0, NOTELL) before increasing monster speed. The resist annotation is therefore downstream of the missing caller invocation, not evidence of a separate resist defect.
